Primary: CNBC quote endpoint, read 07:20:09 BST. Cross-check: Trading Economics (UK 10Y, US 10Y, gold, Brent, GB100).

*** OIL HAS GIVEN BACK MOST OF FRIDAY'S SPIKE, AND THAT IS THE STORY IN THE TICKER ***
Brent 107.61, down 2.05% against Friday's 109.86 settle. Friday it rose 3.72% on the Hormuz escalation
and touched 110 for the first time since May; it closed Sunday's reopen at 108.82, down 0.95%, and has
fallen further overnight. More than half of Friday's gain is now gone. Trading Economics independently
reports -1.99%, which corroborates the MOVE closely even though its level is unusable (see below).
Everything else is quiet: gold firmer, bitcoin up sharply, bonds a shade lower, sterling flat.

London opens at 08:00, twenty minutes after this read, and the feed has lagged the open by up to
forty-five minutes every day this week. The FTSE will be re-read immediately before publication and
this file updated if it has gone live. Trading Economics confirms the FTSE is still shut: its GB100
page returns 10,881.90 "as of Oct/16", i.e. Friday.

*** BITCOIN: A REAL OVERNIGHT MOVE, AND THE PREVIOUS-CLOSE FIELD SHIFTED UNDER IT ***
82,712, up 2.29%. Note the endpoint's previous_day_closing for bitcoin has moved from 81,478.16 last
night to 80,861.21 this morning, which is what a rolling 24-hour basis does on a continuously traded
instrument rather than a fault. Our own published series is the sanity check: 81,665 at 23:59 last
night to 82,712 now is a rise of about 1.3% on our own numbers, against the 2.29% the endpoint reports
on its rolling basis. The endpoint's figure is published because it is the one with a stated basis,
and the discrepancy is recorded here rather than smoothed away.

*** GILT AND TREASURY: BOTH LIVE, BOTH MARGINALLY LOWER, PROVIDERS WITHIN A BASIS POINT ***
  Gilt  CNBC 5.3693, change -0.0072 | Trading Economics 5.36, change -0.015 | our series 5.38 -> 5.37
  UST   CNBC 5.071,  change -0.027  | Trading Economics 5.08, change -0.010 | our series 5.08 -> 5.07
PUBLISHED: Gilt 5.37, -0.01 and UST 5.07, -0.01. In both cases the level is taken from CNBC, which is
the more precise, and the change from our own published series, which sits between the two providers'
figures. That is the rule applied all week when providers disagree by a basis point or two.

*** BRENT: TRADING ECONOMICS UNUSABLE FOR THE LEVEL FOR A FIFTH CONSECUTIVE DAY ***
Its Brent page returns 99.39, about eight dollars below CNBC, continuing a fault first noticed on
Thursday. Its change of -1.99% against CNBC's -2.05% is close, so the direction and size are
corroborated and the level is discarded. Brent rests on CNBC alone, declared, as it has all week.
